title: The Truth of the Shackles
next_chapter_hook: The truth of Chen Nian's imprisonment is tightly bound to blood relative's fate. Chen Ji is caught in a dilemma—his sister is both the Heavenly Fate Lock and the key to breaking the deadlock.

text.content: Golden characters danced on the yellowed page, writhing like living things. Chen Ji stared at that line of text, feeling something burning violently in his chest—thirty years of lifespan, three decades of yang life, exchanged for a single moment of Heavenly Secrets freedom. What a "fair" deal. He laughed bitterly in his heart, though his knuckles unconsciously tightened around his sleeve. The night wind of Tianqing Sect had never been so biting, penetrating the rough cloth of the servant disciple's garments, stabbing straight into his bone marrow. Distant footsteps of the night patrol disciples echoed, and he instinctively pressed the Tianji Record against his chest, his face wearing that familiar expression of timidity.

Thirty years of life, exchanged for a moment of freedom. No matter how you calculate this, it's a losing deal. Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, but didn't refuse immediately. He remembered what Mo Xiansheng had once said—"Every page of the Tianji Record hides a cost." So whose cost was this page set by? Was it the Heavenly Dao, fate, or... He took a deep breath and placed his palm over the page. Ripples of bloodline memory spread from his palm. He was about to do something he'd never tried before—to trace the creator's memory, to see what the shackles originally looked like.

In an instant, the world spun. Chen Ji's consciousness fell into a chaotic torrent, countless images flickering past like a carousel—he saw the life of Chen Xuan, the ancestral father of the Chen Family. He saw a spirited young man obtaining the Tianji Record Fragment in an ancient ruin; he saw that young man cultivate for a hundred years, eventually becoming a master; and then, he saw a world-shaking conspiracy. Chen Ji's heart contracted violently—in that memory, he clearly saw Chen Xuan standing before the Tianji Record, with countless Chen family descendants kneeling behind him. "My Chen family has been a chess piece of the Heavenly Dao for generations," Chen Xuan's voice was old and weary, "Since we cannot escape this fate, then... let those who come after me bear it for me."

dialogue.content: "You've seen it." Mo Xiansheng's voice came from the void, carrying an indescribable sorrow, "Chen Xuan saw through the Heavenly Secrets back then, knowing his end was near. He had two choices—one was to destroy the Tianji Record, allowing the Chen family to completely escape this shackle; the second was... to turn it into a more intricate prison, making future generations guard that elusive Heavenly Dao's grace for him. He chose the latter." Chen Ji felt浑身发冷, and in that memory, he saw Chen Xuan using his finger as a pen and blood as ink, engraving one restriction after another onto the Tianji Record. Each one was a shackle.

text.content: The memory continued to flow. Chen Ji saw Chen Xuan, at the moment his energy was exhausted, sealing a wisp of his residual soul into the first page of the Tianji Record—that was the origin of Mo Xiansheng. "I have become a demon," Chen Xuan murmured in his final moments, "but I do not regret it. Chen family's children, I'm sorry." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, his fingernails digging deep into his palms, blood dripping into the void. He saw the truth now. The Tianji Record was not some precious inheritance—it was a shackle, a shackle forged by Chen Xuan himself, using the entire Chen family's bloodline as material. And they, these descendants, were merely watchdogs he left behind. "What a fine ancestor, what a fine Chen Xuan." A low, hoarse laugh escaped in Chen Ji's heart, laughter filled with bone-piercing coldness.

Rage spread like wildfire in his chest. Chen Ji longed to tear the Tianji Record to shreds, to smash Chen Xuan's memorial tablet to pieces. But just as he was about to lose control, a faint light emerged from the depths of the memory. That was the final mark Chen Xuan left—not a restriction, but a... testament? "If descendants see this book," the old voice echoed in the void, carrying a warmth Chen Ji had never heard before, "If you are wise enough, you will discover a thread of life hidden within the shackle. That is the final insurance I left, and the only way to break the deadlock."

Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, staring fixedly at that point of light. Insurance? That madman Chen Xuan who treated the entire Chen family as chess pieces actually left a backup plan? He forced himself to calm down, listening word by word to that testament. "If you encounter a certain-death situation, the blood relative's life can break it." These eight words exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. His breath suddenly stopped, and a familiar face flashed before his eyes—Chen Nian, his sister who had been missing for years and taken by the Holy Sect. Heavenly Fate Lock. Blood relative's life. All the clues connected at this moment, forming a puzzle that made his entire body go cold.

Chen Nian was not taken by the Holy Sect. Or rather, the Holy Sect was merely carrying out the will of Heaven. Chen Xuan had set this chess move hundreds of years ago, and Chen Nian, from the moment of her birth, was the final chess piece he left behind. Heavenly Fate Lock, capable of breaking the shackle—exchanging a blood relative's life for a thread of hope. Chen Ji felt as if his heart was being tightly gripped by an invisible hand, the pain so intense he could barely breathe. He remembered Chen Nian following him around as a child, remembered the fear and confusion in her eyes when she looked back at him on the day she was taken. So from the very beginning, her existence was merely a key. A key Chen Xuan had prepared long ago, to pry open the shackles.

The memories receded like a tide, and Chen Ji abruptly opened his eyes, finding himself still kneeling in the corner of the Servants' Quarters, his undergarments soaked with cold sweat. The Tianji Record in his arms was slightly scalding, as if mocking his powerlessness. He lowered his head to look at that line of golden text, suddenly finding it utterly ironic. Thirty years of lifespan? Not needed anymore. Because Chen Xuan had long told him—the real cost was not lifespan, but blood relatives. He raised his head, his gaze passing through the broken window lattice, looking toward the depths of Tianqing Sect. Ling Yuan's sleeping quarters were right there. Did that old fox know all this? Or was he too just another piece on Chen Xuan's chessboard?

"So this is your plan?" Chen Ji spoke softly to the Tianji Record, his voice hoarse and unrecognizable, "Let future generations struggle in despair, and finally have to personally kill their own blood relatives to break the deadlock? Chen Xuan, oh Chen Xuan, you truly have excellent calculations." Mo Xiansheng did not respond, as if choosing silence at this moment. Chen Ji didn't expect an answer either. Some truths don't need explanation, only acceptance or resistance. He slowly stood up, pushed open the door of the Servants' Quarters, and night wind howled in, ruffling his robes forcefully. The sky was turning white on the horizon, a new day was about to arrive. And his choice must be made on this day.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji clenched his fist, his mind churning with rage and pain. Facing this chess game left by Chen Xuan, he had to make a choice:

choices.text: Break the Rules—Destroy the Tianji Record
choices.description: Since the Tianji Record was a shackle from the very beginning, destroy it completely. Be neither Chen Xuan's chess piece nor let Chen Nian become a sacrifice.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the ability to foresee the future
choices.risk_hint: Destroying the Tianji Record may trigger unknown backlash, and lose the key trump card against Ling Yuan

text.content: Chen Ji raised the Tianji Record high above his head, spiritual energy gathering in his palm. He stared at the yellowed page, a grim smile tugging at the corner of his lips. "Chen Xuan, did you think you won?" His voice was soft, yet carried undeniable ruthlessness, "I refuse to follow your script." Just as he was about to turn the Tianji Record to ash, a familiar weak voice rang in his mind—it was Mo Xiansheng. "Wait. If you destroy the Tianji Record, your sister will die."

choices.text: Use the Rules—Find a Third Path
choices.description: Since Chen Xuan left insurance, there must be profound meaning. Chen Ji decides to find a way to use the blood relative's life without sacrificing Chen Nian.
choices.visible_cost: Need more time to lay out plans
choices.visible_reward: May find a win-win solution to break the deadlock
choices.risk_hint: Chen Xuan's chess game is profound and unpredictable; any oversight could lead to irretrievable doom

text.content: Chen Ji slowly lowered his raised hand, a cold light flickering in his eyes. Destroy the Tianji Record? That was the inferior strategy. Since Chen Xuan left this move, there would never be only one solution. "Blood relative's life..." he murmured, repeating these four words, his mind racing. Chen Nian was his blood relative, but blood relative didn't necessarily mean her life. Bloodline, lifespan, Heavenly Fate—there must be some connection between these three. He needed more information. "Mo Xiansheng," he spoke, his voice recovering its usual calm, "Did Chen Xuan ever say how this insurance is specifically used?"

Mo Xiansheng remained silent for a long while, so long that Chen Ji thought he wouldn't answer. Finally, that weak voice sounded again, carrying a hint of exhaustion. "He said 'blood relative's fate,' but never specified it must be death." This sentence was like a flash of lightning, cleaving open the fog before Chen Ji's eyes. Not death, but fate—destiny, lifespan, the essence of life. Did Chen Xuan leave this loophole deliberately, or was it his final mercy? He didn't know. But at least, this was a direction. "If I can find a substitute method..." Chen Ji murmured, already formulating a plan in his heart. The Holy Sect took Chen Nian to make a Heavenly Fate Lock Key; Ling Yuan coveted it secretly for the complete Tianji Record. And he would walk a path between these two forces that no one had ever imagined.

The fish-belly white of the dawn gradually tinged with gold, and the melodious sound of the Tianqing Sect's morning bell drifted from afar. Chen Ji tucked the Tianji Record back into his chest, his expression already restored to its usual calm. Only beneath that calm lay a chill unfamiliar even to himself. Chen Xuan had plotted for a thousand years, treating the entire Chen family as chess pieces; he, Chen Ji, was merely a piece of trash, yet he would overturn this chessboard. He remembered when Chen Nian was taken away—she was only twelve, with double buns in her hair, eyes bright as stars. "Brother, when I grow up, I want to protect you." That's what Chen Nian had said back then. Chen Ji closed his eyes, deeply branding those words into his heart. This time, it was his turn to protect her.

Footsteps came from the distance—early-rising servant disciples beginning to sweep the courtyard. Chen Ji skillfully switched to a timid expression, pushed open the door, and passed by a servant on his way out. "Oh, Chen the废物, up so early?" The disciple said with a mocking smile, his tone full of contempt. Chen Ji lowered his head, stammering a reply, and hurried away as if a startled quail. Only after he was far from sight did he faintly curl his lips in an无人处. The废物 persona was the biggest protective color he'd worn all these years. Ling Yuan, Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, Han Lie—every opponent on this chessboard was waiting for him to reveal a flaw. But he wouldn't. At least, not until he rescued Chen Nian.

He needed a plan. The primary goal was to find Chen Nian's whereabouts, next was to understand what the Holy Sect wanted to do with the Heavenly Fate Lock Key, and finally... to find the key that could open Chen Xuan's safe. Three steps, each interlocking, allowing not the slightest error. "Chen Xuan, you think what you gave me is a shackle?" Chen Ji gazed at the rising sun, his eyes reflecting golden light, "Then I'll use this shackle to smash your entire chess game." He silently swore in his heart, then turned toward the Servants' Hall. Today, he still had to be that person everyone could bully—废物 Chen Ji. As for the truth, it would only resurface late at night when all was quiet.

choice.prompt: In the morning light, as Chen Ji was about to head to the Servants' Hall, the Tianji Record in his chest suddenly grew warm. He knew it was Mo Xiansheng calling.

choices.description: Mo Xiansheng is Chen Xuan's remaining soul; perhaps he knows more details about the blood relative's fate. Taking a risk in exchange for key information.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more clues about Chen Xuan's safe
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng's stance is still unclear; he may compromise to Chen Xuan's will

text.content: Chen Ji's footsteps paused; using the motion of tying his shoelaces to observe his surroundings. Confirming no one was watching, he sank his consciousness into the first page of the Tianji Record. Mo Xiansheng's figure appeared in the illusion, his face paler than usual. "You viewed the bloodline memories last night," the old man got straight to the point, "how much did you see?" Chen Ji didn't answer his question, but asked instead: "When Chen Xuan left that safe, did he say anything else? For example, how to 'use' the blood relative's fate?" Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment, finally uttering a word that made Chen Ji's heart pound: "Shared life."

choices.text: "Hold position and go meet Su Qingyao first"
choices.description: Su Qingyao is the only person who noticed something off about him; perhaps her power can be used to gather intelligence on the Holy Sect. Also probe how much she knows about Chen Nian's situation.
choices.visible_reward: Use one force to strike another, while concealing one's true purpose
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao's mind is meticulous; she may in turn extract Chen Ji's secrets

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his hand reaching toward the Tianji Record, and continued toward the Servants' Hall as if nothing had happened. Mo Xiansheng's questions could be asked later; at the moment, there was something more important—he needed to confirm how much Su Qingyao knew about the Holy Sect. Passing through several corridors, he "conveniently" appeared near the sword practice platform where Su Qingyao trained every morning. As expected, that aloof figure was dancing with her sword on the platform, sword light like snow, falling petals profuse. Chen Ji shrunk into a corner, maintaining his usual timidity, but all his attention focused on Su Qingyao. He was waiting for an opportunity, a natural way to approach her.

Su Qingyao sheathed her sword, her gaze like lightning sweeping toward the figure in the corner. She recognized this servant disciple—the one called废物, Chen Ji. Among the many disciples of the Tianqing Sect, this person had almost no presence, low cultivation, mediocre talent, spending all day only sweeping the floor. But somehow, Su Qingyao always felt this person was no simple matter. That feeling was hard to describe, just like... like a wolf hiding among sheep. She slightly frowned, walking a few steps toward Chen Ji. Chen Ji seemed to sense something, his whole body trembling, the broom in his hand "slapping" to the ground. "S...Senior Sister Su!" He knelt行礼 in panic, his voice shaking, "This servant is该死, having disturbed Senior Sister's sword practice!"

dialogue.content: "Get up." Su Qingyao's voice was cold, carrying no emotions whatsoever, "This is my private sword practice platform; why is a servant disciple here?" Chen Ji lowered his head, body shaking like a sieve: "R...Reporting to Senior Sister, this servant is new and didn't know this place was off-limits... this servant will leave immediately!" He frantically picked up the broom, but accidentally tripped, falling狼狈 on the ground. Su Qingyao watched this scene, her brow creasing even tighter. Was she being overly suspicious? This person was clearly just a窝囊废; where was there any abnormality? Just as she was about to turn and leave, her gaze suddenly fell on a small pendant at Chen Ji's waist—a normal peace charm, but the patterns on the talisman... Her pupils constricted sharply. Those were restriction runes only accessible to Inner Sect disciples of the Tianqing Sect.

text.content: Su Qingyao's footsteps abruptly stopped. "Wait." Her voice cooled several degrees, "Where did that peace charm at your waist come from?" Chen Ji acted as if frightened out of his wits, quickly stuffing the peace charm into his chest: "T...This is a legacy from my mother, I...I bought it at the market at the foot of the mountain, it's unrelated to the Sect!" His voice grew smaller and smaller, but his eyes secretly flashed a gleam—he wanted precisely this effect. Su Qingyao stared at him for a long while before finally withdrawing her gaze. "Don't come to this place again." She left these words, turned, and walked away. Chen Ji knelt on the ground until her figure completely disappeared before slowly standing up, a meaningful arc curling at the corner of his mouth. The runes on the peace charm were indeed Inner Sect restrictions, but he hadn't drawn them now—they were stolen from Ling Yuan's study three years ago—one of the chips for later bringing down that old fox.

The first chess piece placed, the probe complete. Su Qingyao had indeed noticed him; though there was no concrete evidence yet, with her personality, she would certainly pay more attention in the future. This was perfect—he needed someone in the light to attract Ling Yuan's attention, and Su Qingyao was the most suitable candidate. Chen Ji shouldered his broom, beginning to sweep like a real servant disciple. But in his mind, he was racing: shared life, blood relative's fate, Heavenly Fate Lock Key... all clues pointed in the same direction—Chen Nian. He silently vowed: Little Nian, wait for Brother. No matter what chess game Chen Xuan had set up, he would smash it to pieces. Because that sister crying alone in the darkness was his only relative in this world, and also his final bottom line.
